# dsh-history-fold
**中文说明：README.zh-CN.md** — 完整对照，含 0.8.0 分类器的实测数据

> **Topics:** `dsh` · `dsh-plugin` · `deepseek-harness` · `persistent-memory` ·
> `long-term-memory`

· `memory-recall` · `history-fold` · `lossless-archive` ·
> `extractive-index` · `recoverable` · `n

recall` · `history-fold` · `lossless-archive` ·
> `extractive-index` · `recoverable` · `non-summary`
**Your assistant remembers yesterday — right up until the context fills up.**

Every conversation that runs long enough hits the same wall: the history no longer fits, so
somethin

g has to be dropped. The built-in compactor drops it by *summarising*, and a summary of
eleven hours

of work is not the parameter you needed, the path you saved, or the decision you
actually made. Ask

about it two days later and you get a confident paraphrase of a memory nobody
kept.

This plugin keeps the whole thing instead. The oldest span of history becomes **one message that
car

ries an extractive index** — real prefixes of the real messages, nothing paraphrased, no model
calle

d — and every folded message is written **verbatim to a local archive first**. The visible
context g
ets short; the history does not disappear.
It is memory, not bookkeeping:

- **Nothing is ever dropped without a copy on disk.** Archive first, fold second; if the write
fails

the fold is abandoned.
- **Nothing is summarised.** The lines in the index are the messages' own pr

efixes, so what the
model sees is quoted evidence, not a rewrite.
- **The notes are regenerable from

your session logs** — delete them entirely and the next refresh
mines them back. Measured below.
## What's new in 0.8.0 — it learned when *not* to interrupt you

Recall only helps if it fires at the right moment. The old gate was a regex: if the message
containe

d a rare identifier or a word like "last time", go look something up. Measured against
**659 hand-la

belled turns** from this project's own 4,906-message history, that regex fired on
**22% of turns tha

t did not need it** — a wall of old notes arriving in the middle of ordinary
conversation.

0.8.0 adds a **659-example classifier** (character n-grams + logistic regression, `lib/gate.js` +
`m
odel/gate-model.json`) that reviews the rule's decision:
| Measured on 659 hand-labelled real turns | Rule alone | With the classifier |

| Turns that genuinely need the archive, admitted | 49/87 (56%) | **51/87 (59%)** |
| Turns that do
Both numbers move the right way — which is the only reason it ships. A filter that bought precision
by giving up recall would have been useless here.

Then the whole decision chain was run over **all 3,431 usable user messages** in that history,
three

he whole decision chain was run over **all 3,431 usable user messages** in that history,
three ways:
| Route | Fires | Fire rate | Tokens injected |

| 0.7 behaviour (strict) | 670 | 19.5% | ≈709k |
| 0.8 rules, no classifier | 2,377 | **69.3%** | ≈2

Without the classifier the plugin was injecting old notes on **one message out of three**.
With it,

the fire rate lands in the 10–15% band where the annotated data says real demand is —
and the inject
ed volume drops **8×**.
The properties that made it shippable rather than merely interesting:
- **1.3 MB, zero dependencies.** Plain JS over a JSON weight table: no ONNX, no runtime, no Python,

no network call, no API cost. Inference is sub-millisecond; total recall overhead is 44–53 ms.
- **A

filter, not an oracle.** It sits on top of the existing rules and can only *veto* them when it
is c

onfident a turn is noise. Explicit recall intent ("what did we decide last time…") never
reaches it.

- **Missing model = unchanged behaviour.** If `model/gate-model.json` is absent or unreadable the

## Requirements / compatibility

**After installing, confirm it actually works — a profile that boots is not proof.**
A plugin can lo

ad cleanly, serve its routes and still break the host; we have seen exactly
that. So the acceptance

test is: **create a new session and send it one message**, then check
`$DSH_HOME/logs/history-fold.j

sonl` for a `profile` line (observer mode) or an
`idle` / `would-fold` / `folded` line. If new sessi

ons cannot be created at all, remove
the mount line above and restart.

Developed and tested against DSH **`0.1.0-rc.7`** — a **customised** build, not a stock
upstream rel

ease. Another version may register its services or name its events differently:
this plugin touches

`ctx.on`, `ctx.effect`, `ctx.tokenMeter`, `ctx.reflect`, `ctx.llm` and the
`agent/pre-step` event.
## Limitations

- Tuned and measured against DeepSeek Harness on Windows with a 1,000,000-token context
window. The

mechanism is adapter-agnostic; the shipped absolute fallbacks are not — which is
what the ratios are

for. When the window resolves, the thresholds scale with it.
- **Whether `ctx.llm` is really reacha

ble from this plugin's context has not been confirmed
against a live DSH.** The lookup mirrors `reso

lveMeter()` (direct property, then
`ctx.reflect.get`, then the agent's own composed context) and nev

er throws, but if no path
works in your build the plugin logs `triggerSource: "default"` and behaves

exactly as it did
before this feature existed.
- Token counts come from DSH's `tokenMeter`. If it i

s unavailable the plugin does nothing —
by design.
- Folding reduces what the model sees. The archiv

e keeps it recoverable, but reading it back
costs a `rg` round-trip.
- It does not (yet) coordinate

with `dsh-compaction-basic`; it simply stays below its
trigger.
